Ось найсвіжіші українські новини за жовтень 2026, які я знайшов. Найостанніші матеріали датовані 16–18 жовтня.

**Головні події**

- **Енергетика та удари:** Російські дрони атакували Луцьк 14 жовтня, є загиблі та поранені. Путін пригрозив Україні ударами у відповідь на атаки по НПЗ, логістичним та енергооб'єктам, про що йдеться 15 жовтня. У Бучанському районі на Київщині 18 жовтня були екстрені відключення світла.
- **Підтримка від партнерів:** Швеція виділила новий пакет допомоги майже на 45 мільйонів євро. Також Україна вперше від початку повномасштабної війни продала газ за кордон.
- **Оборона:** Президент Зеленський за результатами наради з Міноборони затвердив далекобійні санкції на жовтень, як повідомляє 24 Канал.
- **Фінанси:** Кабмін створив комісію для продажу «Сенс Банку» та «Укргазбанку» (18 жовтня). Фонд гарантування вкладів за дев'ять місяців виплатив вкладникам 21,3 мільйона гривень.
- **Кордон:** На українсько-польському кордоні через загрозу атак РФ збільшилися черги (16 жовтня).

**Інше**

- Жовтень має принести рішення щодо бюджету та воєнного стану, а також, можливо, нові мирні переговори. Про це пише Daily.com.ua у підсумках вересня.
- Ukrainian sports: «Шахтар» у Лізі чемпіонів має зіграти в гостях з «Інтером» 21 жовтня.
- Ще один сюжет: у Києві затримали юнака, який, за підозрою, намагався активувати для РФ 148 пристроїв Starlink.

Джерела: Суспільне Новини (архів за 14–16 жовтня), 24 Канал, Укрінформ, Daily.com.ua. Деталі варто перевіряти безпосередньо на сайтах, оскільки стрічки оновлюються щодня.

Here's what the search turned up for Ukraine news in mid-October 2026. Most of it is from the last day or two, and these are headlines and snippets, so I haven't verified the full stories.

**Peace diplomacy and US relations**
- Zelensky says the U.S. and Ukraine are in "constant communication" and are preparing their "next steps", after a call with Trump's peace envoys. One headline frames the call as coming while the US is pivoting to Moscow's side.
- The United States has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine, Zelensky said, after suspending the exchange for a period of time.
- Another headline reports Zelenskyy reacting to Trump's decision to suspend sanctions on Russia.
- Congress is reportedly furious over frozen Russia sanctions but can't respond quickly.
- Ukraine's foreign minister Sybiha said Moscow has failed to honor any commitments on an energy ceasefire.

**Fighting and Russian strikes**
- Russian drones hit western Ukraine in nationwide attacks that killed 10 and injured 73.
- A Russian strike on a residential building in Zaporizhzhia killed a 27-year-old woman.
- Russia struck energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Vinnytsia region, triggering emergency blackouts.
- Emergency workers extinguished a fire in a multi-storey residential building in Odesa after a Russian attack.
- Ukraine's Defense Forces denied Russian claims that Russian troops captured Malokaterynivka in the Zaporizhzhia region.

**Ukrainian strikes on Russia**
- A massive Ukrainian drone attack hit an oil facility, bridge, and data center in St. Petersburg. St. Petersburg's governor confirmed fires at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchyi oil depot, and industrial warehouses.
- A separate headline reports drones attacking Moscow and St. Petersburg and hitting a key oil terminal.

**Europe**
- Europe is planning its first drills for a potential peacekeeping mission in Ukraine.
- Hungary's prime minister announced a decision on Ukrainian grain transit.
- Lithuania foiled an arson attack on Starlink equipment and suspects Russian involvement.
- Poland's prime minister Tusk warned of a major escalation in Russia's hybrid war against Europe.

For full coverage, the Kyiv Independent live page and Ukrinform's latest news feed are the most up to date. I can run a narrower search on any of these threads, such as the peace talks or the sanctions dispute.

**June 3, 2026:** Ukrainian long-range drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg and set it ablaze, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, during the city's annual economic forum. The drones flew more than 1,000 kilometers (600 miles) to hit the terminal, according to Zelenskyy. Russian authorities said only that the Ukrainian drone strike targeted the city's infrastructure, without providing further details. The airport of St. Petersburg briefly suspended flights overnight because of the attack.

**Context:** Ukraine has repeatedly targeted oil facilities at the port of St. Petersburg and nearby ports. The most recent episode is from early October 2026, and Zelensky responded sharply.

The US temporarily lifted sanctions on the sale and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel until 7th of April, 2027. The White House framed it as a way to lower fuel prices. He also argued that "At precisely the moment when we are talking about peace, America is allowing Russia to export diesel."

Reports on the October 14, 2026 strike in Lutsk give different death tolls, which rose as the day went on. The most recent figure I found is six.

- **Early reports (3 dead):** Reuters reported Russian attack on Ukraine's western city of Lutsk on Wednesday killed three and injured at least 12, the regional governor said. Debris from the drone hit a warehouse, and a residential building was damaged as well.
- **Middle update (4 dead):** Ukrainian outlets reported that the drone hit the "EuroGurt" hypermarket on Koniakyna Street. Four people were killed and ten others were injured as a result of the strike. The Volyn police gave this count, and the death toll later rose to four.
- **Latest reports (6 dead):** Ukraine's State Emergency Service said six people were killed and 12 injured, including a child, in Russian attacks on civilian sites in Lutsk on Wednesday, Oct. 14. Kyiv Independent, citing regional governor Roman Romaniuk, similarly reported that the strike killed six people and injuring 10 others. Kyiv Post also reported six killed and 13 injured in Lutsk, as part of a wider attack that day.

Other details are consistent across sources. A nine-story residential building on Sobornosti Avenue was damaged, and a ninth-floor apartment caught fire. Two people were injured, including a child. The attack was part of a larger overnight and daytime assault. Russian forces launched at least 269 drones against Ukraine overnight and throughout Wednesday, Oct. 14.

Because the figures changed over the day, the six-fatality count from the later updates is probably the most current, but it's worth checking official Ukrainian sources for any final count.

Several stories from October 17, 2026 involve Zelensky, mostly about Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy grid and a dispute with Washington over sanctions.

- **Energy strikes:** Russian attacks killed seven people and injured about 90 over the previous day, according to regional authorities. The country reported one of the heaviest Russian attacks against energy infrastructure so far. Zelensky said Russian forces targeted more than 15 key power generation and transmission facilities across Ukraine.
- **US sanctions dispute:** Zelensky criticized Washington for setting aside the sanctions bill named after Senator Lindsey Graham, which he said was meant to apply real pressure on Moscow. He warned the move could aid Russian efforts to disrupt Ukraine's energy supply before winter. The Hill reported that President Trump placed a hold on Russian sanctions days before they were set to go into effect.

He said Ukrainian forces cannot use Starlink or Starshield to intercept jet-powered drones because of a "speed limit" of 161 kilometers per hour.

The Kyiv Independent's homepage also carries items dated October 18, including a report that the U.S. and Ukraine are in "constant communication" and are preparing their next steps. Those fall outside October 17, so treat them as later context.

content.text:
I'd rank these as the three biggest Ukraine stories from 12–19 October 2026:

1. **US–Ukraine rift over Russia sanctions:** Trump put a hold on new Russia sanctions, including the bill named after Senator Lindsey Graham, days before they were due to take effect, a week after easing sanctions on Russian diesel; Zelensky called this a reward for Putin and said Ukraine is "ready to negotiate anywhere" with the US. ([The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/international/6156034-zelensky-open-us-negotiations/))

2. **Russia's attack on Ukraine's power grid:** Around 16–17 October, Russia hit more than 15 key power generation and transmission sites in what Zelensky called one of its largest attacks on the energy system, and the strikes that day killed seven people and injured about 90. ([Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/russian-attacks-kill-7-injure-dozens-across-ukraine-amid-continued-strikes-on-energy-infrastructure/))

3. **Deadly strike on Lutsk:** On 14 October, as part of a wave of at least 269 drones, a Russian drone hit a hypermarket in Lutsk in western Ukraine, killing six people and injuring about a dozen, according to later reports. ([Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/russian-drone-attack-on-western-ukraine-kills-3-injures-20-in-lutsk-and-rivne/))

Choosing the top three is my judgment. A close fourth was Zelensky saying on 17 October that Ukraine's Starlink access is still partly restricted ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/17/zelensky-starlink-elon-musk-trump)). These summaries come from search results rather than full articles, and the Lutsk death toll was rising throughout the day of the attack.
